caveats: Published months describe regional practice across cultivars, management and years; the model uses one 0.5 x 0.625 degree grid cell with one UF-type low-chill southern-highbush parameter set.
Northern-highbush and rabbiteye regions are included to expose transfer limits; disagreement there can reflect species differences rather than weather errors.
Grid minimum temperatures run warm against stations in earlier pilots, so chill and freeze are likely undercounted, most at deciduous and high-elevation sites.
The model assumes open field. Where tunnels are common (protection column), published harvest starts earlier and runs longer than open-field weather implies.
Expectations were compiled from sources before comparison and were not tuned to the model. They are not independent field validation.

November rain and hail (10-12 Nov 2022)
Drought (2021/22, FAS)

sites.name: Osorno / Purranque (Los Lagos)
sites.coordinate_basis: Osorno city centre (below 300 m). Osorno is one of the agroclimates in the UACh fertilization manual.
sites.system_evidence: Southern zone (38°15'-43°40'S): 1,200-2,500 CH, 1,000-2,000 mm rain, volcanic acid soils; plants set in spring (Retamales, FT). The UACh/FIA manual (FT) lists Elliott, Brigitta and Legacy as the main southern cultivars. Annual winter pruning and frost-control systems are standard in the south.
known_weather_risks: November frosts (intense frosts in Nov 2012 made yield predictions overestimate by 55%)
Summer rain (rainfall mainly winter-spring but often in summer, Retamales)
Leaf and fruit sunburn (shade nets under test, Retamales)
Water deficit Oct-Mar at the Osorno and Carillanca agroclimates (UACh manual)

sources.title: Pinochet, Artacho & Maraboli 2014, Manual de fertilización de arándanos cultivados en el sur de Chile (UACh, proyecto FIA PYT 2009-0080)
sources.supports: In the south, Brigitta and Legacy are harvested from late December to late February and Elliott from mid-January to early April. Annual winter pruning and frost-control systems are standard. Intense frosts in Nov 2012 caused 55% overestimation of yield. Osorno and Carillanca have a 5-6 month water deficit (Oct-Mar). National supply peaks Jan-Feb. Petal fall is the stage most vulnerable to frost.

sources.title: Retamales et al. 2014
sources.supports: South region: 1,200-2,500 CH; plants set in spring at 1.0-1.2 x 3 m; harvest late January to early March for the older Elliott and Brightwell base; shade nets tested to delay harvest and prevent sunburn; rain often in summer.

sources.title: USDA FAS GAIN CI2022-0030
sources.supports: Los Lagos 971 ha; Los Ríos 1,616 ha.

sites.name: Zapotlán el Grande (Ciudad Guzmán) / Zapotiltic / Tuxpan
sites.coordinate_basis: Ciudad Guzmán town centre. Elevation 1,507 m from es.wikipedia 'Ciudad Guzmán', which gives 1,507 m a.s.l.; the city sits at the 1,500 m contour.
sites.system_evidence: FAS (FT): harvest timing is set by management. Harvest historically began in early October and peaked in late April to early May. For 2024-25 growers delayed plantings and fertiliser to push the start to February. All production is under plastic with 25% UV shade, about half in 7-10 L substrate pots, and 74% of area is proprietary varieties (Biloxi 23%). Jalisco harvested 2,327 ha in 2022.
known_weather_risks: Intense sunlight; all production is under 25% UV-shade plastic (FAS)
Water scarcity and drought; growers adopting substrate pots, efficient irrigation and private reservoirs (FAS 2025)

sources.title: USDA FAS GAIN MX2024-0003 Blueberry Annual Mexico
sources.supports: Historically harvest began in early October and peaked late April to early May. For 2024, producers delayed the start to early February by delaying new plantings and fertiliser. All production under plastic with 25% UV shade and no open production; half in substrate pots. Jalisco 2,327 ha harvested (2022). Biloxi 23%, proprietary 74%. SIAP stopped reporting after 2022.

sources.title: USDA FAS GAIN MX2025-0004
sources.supports: Harvest start pushed from October to February; February-May revenue window; 19-27 t/ha; water scarcity driving substrate pots.

sources.title: ProducePay: Blueberry producing regions in Mexico (SIAP 2021)
sources.supports: Zapotlán el Grande was the top municipality: 10,394 t, 619 ha (snippet only).

sites.name: Los Reyes de Salgado
sites.coordinate_basis: Los Reyes city centre, 19°35'30"N 102°28'35"W, from the municipal government page (losreyesmichoacan.gob.mx). Elevation 1,325 m from the same page.
sites.system_evidence: Practitioner cycle for Los Reyes (FT, industry). Pruning is in May-June after harvest, followed by 5-6 months of vegetative growth. Floral differentiation is induced by cutting N and reducing irrigation by up to 50%. Bloom starts late October or November and is concentrated in November. Harvest runs from late January to May or June, targeted at a March peak, about 70 days from bloom to harvest. FAS: Michoacán is one of 4 states with 90% of output; all Mexican production is under plastic.
known_weather_risks: Frost; sites where frost is a constant risk are avoided (practitioner)
Rust pressure during vegetative growth (preventive fungicides)
Root waterlogging and fungal disease in saturated beds

sources.supports: Bloom begins late October or November in the Los Reyes area, targeted to concentrate in November. Harvest from late January to May or June, peak targeted in March, about 70 days bloom to harvest. Pruning generally May-June. Induction by N cut and 50% water reduction. Frost site selection, rust, waterlogging.

sites.name: Famaillá / Lules / Monteros (Tucumán piedmont)
sites.coordinate_basis: Famaillá town centre, 27°3'S 65°24'W, 339 m a.s.l. (Infoclima/EcuRed snippet; general gazetteer). Monteros, the EEAOC piedmont reference site, is about 25 km S.
sites.system_evidence: The NOA starts the Argentine season with very early SHB (Snowchaser, Emerald, Springhigh, Ventura) harvested Aug-Oct (SENASA, FT). A 2020 national sector report puts NOA harvest in weeks 33-47, mid-August to late November (FT). EEAOC says piedmont supply falls in September-November (FT). In mid-July 2024, frost damaged small fruits in piedmont orchards while flowering continued, and sprinkler frost protection is used (EEAOC via La Gaceta, FT). So flowering and fruit set overlap mid-winter with little dormant period. The semi_evergreen label is an inference [INFERENCE].
known_weather_risks: Winter frost during bloom and early fruit (July 2024 frosts damaged small fruits in the piedmont; sprinkler frost protection used)
Late frost (12 Sep 2014, -2.3 C, recorded at Tafí del Valle)

sources.title: SENASA / Argentina.gob.ar (Jan 2026): En 2025 se certificó exportación de más de 4200 t de arándanos desde Entre Ríos
sources.supports: NOA (Tucumán, Salta) harvests August-October with Snowchaser, Emerald, Springhigh and Ventura. About 3,500 ha nationally, all SHB.

sources.title: Dirección de Producción Agrícola (MAGyP) Oct 2020: Arándanos, evolución de los principales indicadores
sources.supports: NOA produces from week 33 to 47 (mid-August to late November). National exports: 99% Sep-Dec, peak October (45%), then November (43%). Tucumán had 1,354 of 2,887 ha.

sources.title: Lobo Zavalía et al. 2018, Rev. Ind. Agric. Tucumán 95(2) (EEAOC)
sources.supports: Tucumán's production currently falls in September, October and November. Monteros is the piedmont quality reference site.

sources.title: La Gaceta (19 Jul 2024): Heladas: también se afectaron frutas y verduras (EEAOC Horticultura)
sources.supports: July 2024 frosts affected small blueberry fruits in the piedmont; flowering was not affected at Las Mesadas; plantations with sprinkler frost protection suffered much less.

sources.title: EEAOC Reporte Agroindustrial 25: El arándano en Tucumán
sources.supports: 2008 frosts cost 50% of potential yield; a delayed October harvest concentrated volume in November (PDF returns 403).

The October peak rests on the national export peak (45% in Oct) and a SNIP La Gaceta 2005 statement that 60% of Tucumán fruit is produced in October. Pruning months for the piedmont were not found.

verification.notes: Elevation corrected from 370 to 339 m (gazetteer snippet), with the coordinate rounded to the town (27°3'S 65°24'W). Peak changed from Sep-Oct to Oct. Bloom moved from SNIP-only (thesis snippet) to an FT press report of July fruit and flowering. Harvest months confirmed with an added FT government source.

sites.name: Tafí del Valle (EEAOC substation)
sites.coordinate_basis: Tafí del Valle town centre (-26.8517, -65.7098, gazetteer snippet). Elevation 2,000 m from es.wikipedia 'Valle de Tafí' (snippet). The paper's site table is an image and could not be read.
sites.system_evidence: EEAOC collection of 15 high-chill cultivars (500-1,200 CH: NHB, SHB, RE) planted in October 2010 in an intermontane valley. Buds swell from September and bloom from October, escaping the mean last-frost date. Summer pruning removes the fruited canes; winter pruning removes 20% of woody stems. The site is experimental; the paper proposes the valleys as a new production zone.
known_weather_risks: Late spring frost: 12 Sep 2014, -2.3 C absolute minimum, affected flowering and cut yields of all 15 cultivars
Limited irrigation water (10-day turns, 15 mm per application Sep-Dec)

sources.title: Lobo Zavalía, Berettoni, Forns & Ale 2018, Rev. Ind. Agric. Tucumán 95(2) (EEAOC)
sources.supports: Planted October 2010. Bud swell from September, flowering from October. First fruit in the first week of December; harvest peaks in January-February. Bluegold 2nd week Dec to 1st week Feb; Bluecrop and Legacy 1st week Jan to 2nd week Feb; Ochlockonee 3rd week Jan to 3rd week Mar; Powderblue 3rd week Jan to 2nd week Mar. Frost on 12 Sep 2014 (-2.3 C). Summer and winter pruning. Irrigation every 10 days.

sites.notes: Only high-chill phenology dataset in Argentina. Planting month is the trial planting. Commercial area in the valleys is small; the paper frames them as a potential new zone.

verification.notes: All months, the frost event and pruning were confirmed in full text. Coordinates refined to the gazetteer town centre. The 2,000 m elevation is supported by a Wikipedia search snippet, not by the paper; accepted with that caveat.

sites.name: Concordia
sites.coordinate_basis: Concordia city centre (INTA EEA Concordia; below 300 m).
sites.system_evidence: INTA Concordia (FT, RIA 2012): commercial Misty, Jewel and Emerald farms in the Concordia department reached full bloom on 15 Aug 2008. They were managed with fertigation, sprinkler frost control and summer pruning. The INTA chapter abstract (ABS) describes highbush with deciduous leaves that colour with chill during winter dormancy, pruned in winter, spring or both. The NEA is the country's main volume zone (SENASA). SHB low-chill with winter dormancy and a late-winter bloom corresponds to the deciduous system. Snowchaser 'evergreen management' appears only in a snippet.
known_weather_risks: Late-winter frost on early SHB bloom (plants that satisfy chill early are exposed to late-winter frosts, INTA via MAGyP; sprinkler frost control is standard)
Adverse winter and early-spring weather: 2026 harvest delayed with estimated losses up to 35% (press snippet)

sources.title: Rivadeneira 2012, Concentración de nutrientes en hojas de arándano (RIA 38(3), INTA Concordia)
sources.supports: Two commercial farms in the Concordia department. Full bloom on 15/08/2008 for Misty, Jewel and Emerald. Management included fertigation, sprinkler frost control and summer pruning. 1,158 ha in Concordia in 2011.

sources.title: SENASA / Argentina.gob.ar (Jan 2026)
sources.supports: NEA (Concordia, Corrientes) main volume September-November with Emerald, Star, Kestrel and Flicker. More than 4,200 t certified from Entre Ríos in 2025/26.

sources.title: Dirección de Producción Agrícola (MAGyP) Oct 2020
sources.supports: NEA harvest weeks 37-49 (mid-September to early December). National export peak October (45%) and November (43%). INTA note that early chill satisfaction exposes plants to late-winter frosts. 825 ha in Entre Ríos, mainly Concordia.

sources.title: Rivadeneira (INTA Concordia) 2022, Características botánicas, variedades, poda y manejo del cultivo en arándano
sources.supports: Highbush has deciduous leaves that colour with chill in winter dormancy. Pruning in winter, spring or both. (The PDF fetch aborted; a snippet says bloom is induced in late winter or early spring and lasts 3-6 weeks.)

sources.title: Entre Ríos Ya (Sep 2026): cosecha de arándanos estiman pérdidas de hasta 35%
sources.supports: 2026 harvest delayed with 30-35% loss from winter and early-spring weather (press snippet).

sites.notes: Main bloom is August (full bloom 15 Aug in the 2008 INTA observation; the snippet gives a 3-6 week bloom period). Pruning is summer, post-harvest (INTA 2012). The hail and hail-net claim was not verified and has been dropped.

verification.notes: Bloom corrected from Aug-Sep (snippet) to August, based on an FT INTA observation. Harvest extended to December (NEA weeks 37-49, FT). System changed from semi_evergreen (inference) to deciduous, based on FT and ABS evidence of winter dormancy, frost control and summer pruning. The cultivar-share figures (Emerald 32%, Snowchaser 26%) were snippet-only and removed.

sites.name: Guasca (Sabana de Bogotá highlands)
sites.coordinate_basis: Guasca town centre. The trial latitude (4°52.868'N) matches the town; the paper's longitude (74°29.733'W) falls west of Bogotá and appears to be an error. Elevation: 2,700 m in both the paper and es.wikipedia 'Guasca (Cundinamarca)'.
sites.system_evidence: Commercial open-field Biloxi and Sharpblue at 2,700 m. Mean temperature 12.85 C (10.6-17.0), RH 84.9%, 641 mm bimodal rain. Pruning every two months. Fruit was harvested weekly for 28 consecutive weeks (Jun-Dec 2014), and the authors note that harvest was continuous, unlike the single annual season reported elsewhere. Harvest peaks followed flowering peaks that were probably triggered by low-rain periods.
known_weather_risks: High humidity (84.9% mean RH); rust and grey mould observed
Harvest peaks tied to dry spells that induce bloom; flowering is not synchronised by season

sources.title: Cortés-Rojas et al. 2016, Yield and fruit quality of Biloxi and Sharpblue in Guasca, Colombia (Agronomía Colombiana 34(1))
sources.supports: 2,700 m; Tmean 12.85 C; RH 84.87%; 640.8 mm bimodal rain; open field on raised beds with plastic mulch and fertigation; pruning every two months; mites, rust and grey mould; 28 weekly harvests Jun-Dec 2014, continuous; peaks linked to low-rain periods; 25 ha in Cundinamarca and Boyacá.

sources.title: es.wikipedia: Guasca (Cundinamarca)
sources.supports: Municipality at 2,700 m a.s.l., mean temperature 15 C, 50 km NE of Bogotá.

sites.notes: Evergreen pruning is continuous (every two months). Year-round bloom and harvest are extrapolated from 28 weeks of continuous harvest (Jun-Dec) plus the authors' statement that continuous production is possible [partly INFERENCE for Jan-May]. Peak months are undefined.

verification.notes: Trial details confirmed in full text; elevation cross-checked with Wikipedia. Removed the unsourced 'hail and cold nights' risk. Dropped the unread 2023 cost-analysis snippet.

sites.name: Vacaria (Campos de Cima da Serra)
sites.coordinate_basis: Vacaria town centre, 28°30'44"S 50°56'02"W, 971 m a.s.l. (pt.wikipedia 'Vacaria').
sites.system_evidence: Commercial planting began in 1990 at Vacaria with highbush (Italbraz). Vacaria and Caxias do Sul held 20.2 ha of RS area in the Embrapa table. The Vacaria-São José dos Ausentes highlands are among the coldest areas of southern Brazil and suit chill-demanding cultivars. Highbush needs 650-800 CH, and lack of chill causes poor budbreak and bloom (Embrapa, FT). Transplanting is done in winter dormancy (Embrapa via Revista Cultivar, FT).
known_weather_risks: Frost during bloom (frost tolerance at bloom is a breeding target, Embrapa)
Fruit cracking in wet periods in rabbiteye (Embrapa)
Insufficient chill in mild winters causing poor budbreak and bloom (Embrapa)

sources.title: Embrapa Uva e Vinho & Embrapa Clima Temperado, 'Grande potencial' (Revista Cultivar, 2015)
sources.supports: Italbraz highbush at Vacaria from 1990; 75% of Brazilian area in RS, especially Vacaria. Brazilian harvest normally November-April. Transplant in winter dormancy. Regions with more than 500 CH preferred; under 300 CH problematic.

sources.title: Embrapa Clima Temperado, Sistema de Produção do Mirtilo (Sistema de Produção 8)
sources.supports: Commercial planting started in 1990 at Vacaria; Vacaria 13.2 ha in the RS table. The Vacaria-São José dos Ausentes highlands are the coldest region. Highbush needs 650-800 CH; lack of chill causes deficient budbreak and bloom. Rabbiteye fruit cracks in wet periods. Frost tolerance during bloom is a breeding objective. Winter and green pruning.

sources.title: Embrapa Uva e Vinho: Fenologia e aptidão de cultivares de mirtilo (Vacaria)
sources.supports: Bloom periods Aug-Nov across SHB, RE and NHB cultivars at Vacaria (snippet only; page returns 403).

sites.notes: Bloom months rest on a snippet (low confidence). The Nov-Apr harvest is Embrapa's national statement, not Vacaria-specific. No Vacaria peak was found.

verification.notes: Elevation corrected from 955 to 971 m (Wikipedia). The Revista Cultivar article credits Embrapa Uva e Vinho and Clima Temperado; the named authors Hoffmann & Antunes come only from Epagri's citation. Bloom is kept at low confidence because it is snippet-only.

sites.name: Pelotas (Estação Experimental Cascata, Embrapa Clima Temperado)
sites.coordinate_basis: Cascata experimental station, 31°37'15.57"S 52°31'30.77"W, 164 m (Antunes et al. 2008), in Pelotas' colonial zone about 25 km NW of the city centre. The trial site is used because the phenology comes from there.
sites.system_evidence: Rabbiteye cultivars (8 in the trial) show winter dormancy, with bloom starting in the first or second half of August. Rabbiteye is recommended for southern RS because it needs one-third to one-half of the highbush chill (Embrapa, FT). Winter pruning is practised and plants are transplanted in winter.
known_weather_risks: Insufficient or variable winter chill (harvest length varied with inter-annual temperature; deficient chill gives poor budbreak and bloom)
Rain during ripening cracks rabbiteye fruit (Embrapa)

sources.title: Antunes et al. 2008, Fenologia, produção e qualidade de frutos de mirtilo (Pesq. Agropec. Bras. 43(8))
sources.supports: Cascata station at 164 m. Eight RE cultivars over 2003/04-2005/06. Bloom begins in the first or second half of August and ends between the second half of September and the first half of October. Harvest averages 37 days, between December and January.

sources.title: Embrapa Clima Temperado, Sistema de Produção do Mirtilo
sources.supports: 2003 Pelotas cultivar table: bloom starts 18-21 Aug, ends 28 Sep-14 Oct; maturation 24 Nov-21 Jan. RE recommended for southern RS. Fruit cracking in wet periods. Winter pruning.

sources.title: Embrapa via Revista Cultivar, 'Grande potencial'
sources.supports: Transplant in winter during dormancy; RE introduced at Pelotas in 1983.

sites.notes: Useful test of rabbiteye's long bloom-to-harvest interval (August bloom, December harvest). Some cultivars begin maturing in late November (Embrapa 2003 table).

verification.notes: Bloom, harvest and site confirmed in full text. The '276 h chill in 2005' figure could not be confirmed (the relevant sentence is truncated in the fetched text) and was removed. The pollination-deficit item was removed because it is not a weather risk.

sites.name: Lages / Planalto Serrano (incl. Palmeira)
sites.coordinate_basis: Lages city centre, 916 m (pt.wikipedia 'Lages'). The Epagri Lages station is at -27.8086, -50.33; its altitude in the zoning table is garbled ('9387,7'). Papanduva (Planalto Norte) was requested, but no locality-specific months were found.
sites.system_evidence: Epagri/Ciram zoning (FT) uses a mean phenology: bloom stimulus 30 days, start to full bloom 30 days, full bloom to end of bloom 20 days, end of bloom to fruit set 20 days, with tolerable frost falling from strong to none. Bloom stimulus falls after 10 Aug at Caçador and after 26 Aug at São Joaquim, once frost probability is below 20%. Highland stations accumulate 538-856 CH. In 2012/13 SC produced 41.4 t on 23.1 ha, with the best yields at Lages and Fraiburgo. A grower in Palmeira near Lages reports bloom in September (press, FT).
known_weather_risks: Frost from full bloom to fruit set (only weak frost tolerated at the end of bloom and none at set; frost classes: weak 3 to 1 C, moderate 1 to -2 C, strong below -2 C)
Water deficit during fruit growth (the crop needs at least 50 mm of water per week)

sources.title: Pandolfo et al. 2017, Zoneamento agroclimático do mirtilo irrigado em Santa Catarina (Agropecuária Catarinense 30(1), Epagri/Ciram)
sources.supports: Station table; phenology phase durations and frost tolerance; bloom stimulus 28 Jun at Chapecó (295 CH), 10 Aug at Caçador (538 CH), 26 Aug at São Joaquim (856 CH); 2012/13 SC crop 41.4 t on 23.1 ha with best yields at Lages and Fraiburgo; 50 mm per week water need; frost classes.

sources.title: Revista Cultivar (Jul 2025): Produção de mirtilo ganha espaço em área reflorestada de SC (Palmeira, near Lages)
sources.supports: A Palmeira grower (about 3,000 plants, Epagri-assisted) reports the orchard 'florada, em setembro'.

sources.title: Portal RBV (Dec 2024): Conheça o Mirtilo (Caçador, SC)

sites.name: Mengzi (Honghe prefecture, southeast Yunnan plateau)

Mengzi picking runs from November to late May/early June under greenhouses with drip fertigation (Xinhua), and Honghe's off-season cycle runs Nov-Apr (IBO), while the rest of China is still in bloom. A continuous winter crop with no dormant period fits an evergreen system. No source explicitly documents evergreen pruning management in Mengzi [INFERENCE].

Rainy season May-Oct degrading fruit quality/harvest of mid-season cultivars; above-average rainfall lowering sweetness (2025)

sites.name: Qingdao West Coast New Area (Huangdao) and Rizhao (Shandong peninsula)
sites.coordinate_basis: Huangdao district centre, Qingdao West Coast New Area. Chentuan (Rizhao), with 1,660 ha and 30% of Shandong output, is the best-documented locality.
sites.system_evidence: Warm temperate monsoon climate with deciduous highbush (Legacy is the core Qingdao cultivar). Heated greenhouse, unheated greenhouse and open field coexist. Heated-greenhouse SHB is picked from mid-late March, unheated greenhouse from late May, and open field peaks in June-July, finishing early July. All are dormant-cycle systems, some forced.
known_weather_risks: Water shortage: 650-850 mm rain vs 1000-1200 mm evaporation, poor groundwater
Hot dry winds in late spring
Freezing in winter and early spring
Summer rainstorms (60% of rain in summer)

sites.name: Dandong (Liaodong peninsula)
sites.coordinate_basis: Dandong city centre; Liaoning government reports Dandong at >25% of national blueberry output (2021)
sites.system_evidence: Temperate continental monsoon climate with 168-180 frost-free days. Open-field NHB (Blomidon, Bluecrop, Duke) is harvested early July to late August, the latest in China, and plants are laid down and soil-covered for winter. Forcing culture in heated greenhouses with early SHB (Misty) is warmed from mid-November and picked mid-late March. The Liaoning Science & Technology Department reports substrate SHB greenhouses bringing fruit to market from February, and extension of low-chill 'evergreen' SHB soilless culture in greenhouses.
known_weather_risks: Winter freeze damage and winter-spring drought (plants must be buried)
Continuous rainy days during the open-field harvest reducing fruit quality
Overcast/snowy spells mid-Jan to early Mar risking fruit chilling injury in greenhouses
